screening_decisions.reason: Multicentre RCT randomising women after surgery for stage I endometrial carcinoma to adjuvant medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) versus no further treatment, or radiotherapy versus radiotherapy plus MPA. It is an RCT of progestagen therapy in women who have had surgery for endometrial cancer.
Narrative review and survey of clinical observations, not a primary RCT. It does not report original randomised trial data meeting the selection criteria.
Methodological paper about measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses. Not an RCT and does not involve progestagen therapy or endometrial cancer patients.
Methodological paper on statistical methods for meta-analysis. Not an RCT and does not involve progestagen therapy or endometrial cancer patients.
Randomised controlled trial of adjuvant progestagen therapy versus no additional therapy after surgery in 1148 patients with Stage I or Stage II endometrial cancer. Meets all selection criteria.
Methodological paper examining meta-analysis approaches for combining results from clinical trials. Not a primary RCT of progestagen therapy in endometrial cancer.

RCT randomising women on diagnosis to progestogen or control as part of primary treatment for endometrial carcinoma in conjunction with surgery and radiotherapy. All patients underwent operation. Meets literal criteria (RCT, progestagen, women who had surgery), though intervention was given as part of primary treatment rather than strictly post-surgery adjuvant.
Methodological paper on extracting summary statistics for meta-analyses with survival endpoints. Not an RCT and does not involve progestagen therapy or endometrial cancer patients.

RCT comparing adjuvant hydroxyprogesterone versus placebo after total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in patients with stage IA or IB endometrial cancer. Meets all selection criteria.
Prospective clinical trial randomly assigning 205 patients to adjuvant progestagen treatment or no additional therapy after hysterectomy for endometrial cancer. Meets all selection criteria.
